title: Super versus 401ks: How do the retirement systems stack up?
full_text:
The Australian superannuation system is widely regarded as one of the best in the world but how do retirement savings compare to United States’ 401ks?
Research by iSelect has compared the median savings of the Australian superannuation members versus those who have a 401k in the United States.
Those individuals aged 55-64 have just US$15,000 ($20,700) in the United States compared to $400,000 in Australia. They also believe they would need US$550,000 ($763,000) in their retirement, largely in line with their Australian counterparts who expect to need $750,000.
In the younger brackets, those aged 35-44 have median savings just US$50,000 compared to $200,000 for Australians. While there is a stark differentiation between their savings, both believe they will need $1 million to retire, indicating Americans have a lot of catching up to do to meet their goal.
Across all age groups, the median savings were US$71,000 in the US and $180,000 in Australia.
The report also noted that 16 per cent of American surveyed have zero retirement savings.
Commenting on the US data, iSelect said: “Surprisingly, those nearing retirement face substantial shortfalls – Americans aged 55-64 reported needing US$550,000 but having only US$15,000 saved. Again, older adults, those aged 65-74 and over 75 also reported needing around US$1million, but their savings remain far lower at US$200,000. Those over 75 years had a substantial US$150,000 saved in comparison.
“Overall, the data highlights a pronounced mismatch between retirement aspirations and actual savings across all age brackets.”
Retirement savings split by age
Source: iSelect, September 2026, exchange rate of 1.38 AUD per 1 USD.
For Australia, it stated: “Overall, the data shows that while retirement expectations remain consistently high across middle age, savings levels lag behind at all ages, suggesting a persistent and widening retirement preparedness gap as individuals move through life.”
More Americans were unsure about their retirement future, highlighting the greater public awareness of the superannuation system in Australia which begins as soon as an individual starts work.
Some 41 per cent of men and 62 per cent of female Americans said they “did not know” how much they would need for retirement compared to 32 per cent of male Australians and 51 per cent of women.
Both Americans and Australians intend to retire at 65.2 years of age, although the Australian state pension is unavailable until they turn 67.
author: Laura Dew
